fixes.explanation: The psalm never mentions priests or an altar. David says he beheld God's "…power and glory." (Psalm 63:2) That's what he names in the sanctuary, and it's the answer for this one. Sounds like he was looking at the right thing.

Trust is a fine word, and it's a good thing to do. But David says something else in verse 3: “…my lips will glorify You.” The word is glorify. Trust is a good friend, but it's sitting in the wrong seat on this one. Lips get the glorifying, and the blank gets that word.

Obey is a good word, friend, but it's not the one David picked here. This verse is about what his lips will do, and he says, “…my lips will glorify You.” Obey is a solid word, but this blank is about lips, and lips here glorify. I once tried to get my own lips to say something this good before breakfast. Didn't happen.

I get why you'd pick it, since David did start out thirsty. Verse 1 says, “my soul thirsts for You.” But verse 5 says, “My soul is satisfied as with the richest of foods…” The psalm doesn't say starving. It says satisfied.

David says, “For You are my help; I will sing for joy in the shadow of Your wings.” God is his help, and that's the reason he gives for singing. He doesn't say he'll sing someday when things calm down. He says he will sing for joy in that shadow.

David says, “But those who seek my life to destroy it will go into the depths of the earth.” That's a heavy line, and it's okay to let it be heavy. The psalm turns here from David's praise to the ones who seek his life. It comes right after David says his soul clings to God.
